notes:
I couldn't do this research, so I don't have any notes on Psalm 34 for you yet.

My web tool stopped working before any page loaded. My first attempt to open Enduring Word, Precept Austin, Bible Hub and New Advent returned an error. A second test call failed the same way: the tool reported that I had no calls left for this turn. My other tool has no internet access, so I couldn't reach any of the approved sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point, and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. Since I didn't read a single page, writing notes from memory would break those rules, so I haven't written any.

Please send the request again in a new message and I'll start over. I plan to look at:

- **Verse-by-verse commentaries:** Enduring Word, Precept Austin, and Bible Hub or StudyLight for Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and Spurgeon's *Treasury of David*.
- **Protestant differences:** each tradition's own teachers where they actually disagree. Likely places are the angel of the LORD (v. 7), "taste and see" (v. 8) and "lack no good thing" (v. 10).
- **Other views:** NET Bible notes on the heading, which names Abimelech rather than Achish, and on the psalm's acrostic form. Catholic and Orthodox readings (it is Psalm 33 in the Greek and Latin numbering), including Augustine on New Advent. How John 19:36 applies v. 20 to Christ. What the sites say about prosperity teaching on v. 10.
